hero.subline: Psychological portraiture, the nude, personal photo projects.

about.label: About me
about.heading:
I believe photography
can see more than
we are used to showing
paragraphs: I have worked in photography since 2012, though I started shooting much earlier. As a child I photographed sunrises, sunsets, flowers, animals and landscapes on a simple film camera. I have always been drawn to watching the world, to noticing what you can walk straight past without ever seeing it.
Over time, a person moved to the centre of my attention. Their face, body, gestures, the way they are in the frame. How we show ourselves to others — and what we cannot, or do not want, to show.

I am a Ukrainian photographer and psychotherapist. My professional path in psychology shaped how I look at a person, although photography for me is a separate space of inquiry. What matters there is presence, form, light, gaze — and the chance to see something there are no words for yet.
I do not try to make a person perfect in the frame. I am more interested in finding an image in which they do not have to meet anyone's idea of beauty, femininity, masculinity or the right body.
Perhaps photography begins for me exactly where the need to prove something ends.

items.title: Psychological portrait
items.text: I am interested not only in how a person looks, but in how they are present in the frame. The gaze, tension and release, habitual gestures, the moments when the need to play a role falls away. I make portraits where what matters is not the pose or the styling, but the person themselves.

items.title: Nude
items.text: The body, for me, is not an object to be corrected or made more attractive. It has its own shape, history, texture and presence. In this work I am drawn to embodiment beyond normative beauty, to vulnerability, strength, ambiguity — and to the way a body becomes an image.

items.title: Personal projects
items.text: This is a space for themes I return to for years. For exploring the body, identity, memory, vulnerability, and what is hard to put into words directly. Here photography can be a document, a metaphor, a question, or a way of staying close to something that has no simple explanation.

items.title: Visual diaries
items.text: Landscapes, plants, animals, light, and the places your mind returns to even after years. This is photography outside of briefs and deadlines — watching the world, a part of my personal archive, a way of keeping what is changing or disappearing.

statement.label: Statement
statement.heading: My photography
statement.quote: Perfection doesn't interest me — life itself does.
paragraphs: I photograph people, but what interests me is not only what can be seen.

I am drawn to the body as part of our story, as a way of being in the world, as something we know more intimately than anything else and can also feel is foreign. I am drawn to beauty that needs no standard to measure up to, and to vulnerability that does not necessarily mean weakness.

My eye was formed at the intersection of photography, psychology and a years-long interest in how a person experiences themselves and meets others. Yet I do not look for a psychological explanation in every image. Sometimes form, light, a gaze or a gesture is enough. Sometimes photography asks more questions than it answers.
I want to leave room for ambiguity. Not to explain everything to the end, not to turn experience into a beautiful story, and not to ask a person to be someone else in order to deserve attention.
Perhaps that is why I return, again and again, to the portrait and the body. To what we show, hide, accept, reject, and try to see anew.
I do not want to repair a person, to make them better, to fit them to an idea of normal. But to look carefully, and to let the image be more complex than a simple explanation.

contact.label: Get in touch
contact.heading:
If my gaze on
photography feels
close to you
paragraphs: If you want to create a portrait, explore your own image, or talk about working together — write to me.
I am open to individual sessions, artistic collaborations, and projects that leave room for curiosity, trust, and the search for your own visual language.
Tell me a little about your idea. You do not need to know yet what the result should be.
